paragraphs: XjLND, O RSghava, when Brahmadatta was married, that sonless one, (Ku^anSbha), with the intention of obtaining male offspring, took in hand a son-conferring sacrifice. And when the sacrifice had commenced, that son of BrahmJL, the exceedingly noble Ku^a, spake unto king Ku^anSbha, saying, — ‘O son, there will be born unto thee a virtuous son like unto thyself : thou wilt obtain even Gadhi, — and through him enduring fame in this world.’ Having said this unto king Ku9anabha 9 Ku^a, O R5ma, entering the welkin, went to the eternal regions of BrahmS. Then after sometime, an eminently virtuous son, named GSdhi, was born unto the intelligent Ku9an£bha. O K&kutstha, even that highly pious G&dhi is my sire. And, O descendant of Raghu I, called Kau9ika, am sprung from Ku9a's line.

And, O xAmAyana. RSghava, I had a sister of noble vows born before me. And her name was Satyavati ; and she was bestowed upon Richika. And following her lord, she ascended heaven in her own proper person. And my highly generous sister, Kau9iki, hath finally assumed the form of a mighty river. And in order to compass the welfare of all creatures, my sister is now a noble and charming river of sacred waters, issuing from the Himavat mountains. And thenceforth, out of affection for my sister, Kou^iki, I ever dwell happily in the vicinity of the Himavat, O Raghava. And that virtuous Kau9iki, Satyavati, as well established in religion as truth, and chaste, and eminently pious, is now the foremost of streams.

And, O Rama it is only for the purpose of completing my sacrifice that leaving her behind, I have come to Siddha9rama. And now by virtue of thy energy, have I attained frution. Now, O R&ma, I have narrated unto thee the circumstances connected with the history of my line and myself, as also of this place, O mighty armed one, — which thou hadst asked me to relate. But, O Kakutstha, while I was speaking, half the night hath been spent. Do thou now sleep, good betide thee, — so that thou mayst not feel any difficulty while on the journey. The trees stand motionless, and the beasts and birds are silent, and, O descendant of Raghu, all sides have become enveloped in nocturnal gloom.

The midnight is gradually passing away ; and the firmament thick-studded with stars resembling eyes, is illumined up with their light. And that dispeller of darkness, the milcF-beaming moon, is rising, gladdening the hearts of all creatures with his splendour. And night-ranging beings — terrible carnivorous Yakshas and P&kshasas — walk hither and thither.” Having said this, the mighty ascetic of exceeding energy paused. And those ascetics honoring him, said, — “ Excellent ! Excellent ! This line belonging to the Ku9*ikas is ever exalted and devoted to virtue, And those foremost of men sprung in the Ku9a race are high-souled and like unto Brahmarshis — and specially thou, O illustrious VicvvSniitra, art so. And that best of streams, Kau^iki, hath added lustre unto thy line.” and the auspicious son of Ku9ika having been extolled by those delighted ascetics— the foremost of their order — slept, like unto the sun, when setting. And Rama too along with Sumitra’s son having in admiration praised that best of ascetics, enjoyed the luxury of slumber.

verses.sa:
कृतोद्वाहे गते तस्मिन् ब्रह्मदत्ते च राघव ।
अपुत्रः पुत्रलाभाय पौत्रीमिष्टिमकल्पयत् ॥

इष्ट्यां तु वर्तमानायां कुशनाभं महीपतिम् ।
उवाच परमोदारः कुशो ब्रह्मसुतस्तदा ॥

पुत्रस्ते सदृशः पुत्र भविष्यति सुधार्मिकः ।
गाधिं प्राप्स्यसि तेन त्वं कीर्तिं लोके च शाश्वतीम् ॥

एवमुक्त्वा कुशो राम कुशनाभं महीपतिम् ।
जगामाकाशमाविश्य ब्रह्मलोकं सनातनम् ॥

कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य कुशनाभस्य धीमतः ।
जज्ञे परमधर्मिष्ठो गाधिरित्येव नामतः ॥

स पिता मम काकुत्स्थ गाधिः परमधार्मिकः ।
कुशवंशप्रसूतोऽस्मि कौशिको रघुनन्दन ॥

पूर्वजा भगिनी चापि मम राघव सुव्रता ।
नाम्ना सत्यवती नाम ऋचीके प्रतिपादिता ॥

सशरीरा गता स्वर्गं भर्तारमनुवर्तिनी ।
कौशिकी परमोदारा सा प्रवृत्ता महानदी ॥

दिव्या पुण्योदका रम्या हिमवन्तमुपाश्रिता
लोकस्य हितकार्यार्थं प्रवृत्ता भगिनी मम ॥

ततोऽहं हिमवत्पार्श्वे वसामि नियतः सुखम्
भगिन्यां स्नेहसंयुक्तः कौशिक्यां रघुनन्दन ॥

सा तु सत्यवती पुण्या सत्ये धर्मे प्रतिष्ठिता
पतिव्रता महाभागा कौशिकी सरितां वरा ॥

अहं हि नियमाद्राम हित्वा तां समुपागतः
सिद्धाश्रममनुप्राप्तः सिद्धोऽस्मि तव तेजसा ॥

एषा राम ममोत्पत्तिः स्वस्य वंशस्य कीर्तिता
देशस्य च महाबाहो यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥

गतोऽर्धरात्रः काकुत्स्थ कथाः कथयतो मम ।
निद्रामभ्येहि भद्रं ते मा भूद् विघ्नोऽध्वनीह नः ॥

निष्पन्दास्तरवः सर्वे निलीना मृगपक्षिणः ।
नैशेन तमसा व्याप्ता दिशश्च रघुनन्दन ॥

शनैर्विसृज्यते संध्या नभो नेत्रैरिवावृतम् ।
नक्षत्रतारागहनं ज्योतिर्भिरवभासते ॥

१-३४-१६॥
उत्तिष्ठते च शीतांशुः शशी लोकतमोनुदः ।
ह्लादयन् प्राणिनां लोके मनांसि प्रभया स्वया ॥

नैशानि सर्वभूतानि प्रचरन्ति ततस्ततः ।
यक्षराक्षससंघाश्च रौद्राश्च पिशिताशनाः ॥

एवमुक्त्वा महातेजा विरराम महामुनिः ।
साधुसाध्विति तं सर्वे मुनयो ह्यभ्यपूजयन् ॥

कुशिकानामयं वंशो महान् धर्मपरः सदा ।
ब्रह्मोपमा महात्मानः कुशवंश्या नरोत्तमाः ॥

विशेषेण भवानेव विश्वामित्र महायशः ।
कौशिकी सरितां श्रेष्ठा कुलोद्योतकरी तव ॥

मुदितैर्मुनिशार्दूलैः प्रशस्तः कुशिकात्मजः ।
निद्रामुपागमच्छ्रीमानस्तंगत इवांशुमान् ॥

रामोऽपि सहसौमित्रिः किञ्चिदागतविस्मयः ।
प्रशस्य मुनिशार्दूलं निद्रां समुपसेवते ॥
